D: Wolverine is sent back to 1973 to stop a choice that dooms mutants in the future.
P: Serve the snacks when Quicksilver races around the Pentagon kitchen in slow motion.
S: Quicksilver's slow-motion run around the Pentagon kitchen
Tomato soup simmered with onion and garlic, blended smooth and served in mugs with grilled cheese fingers.
Choux pastry with gruyère piped into small balls, baked at 200C for 20 minutes until puffed.
Cheddar, cream cheese and spring onion rolled into a ball, coated in chopped walnuts, with crackers.
M: Beef bourguignon of chuck, bacon, mushrooms and red wine simmered 3 hours, with buttery mash.
the showdown on the White House lawn
Burgers and hot dogs grilled for a crowd, served with a potato salad of boiled potatoes, mayo, mustard and spring onion.
W: the 1970s, when fondue parties were everywhere
Dark chocolate melted gently with cream in a fondue pot, kept warm at the table, with strawberries, marshmallows and sponge cubes on forks to dip.
K: Lemonade with blue curaçao or blue cordial over crushed ice with lime.

s.note: Quicksilver's slow-motion run around the Pentagon kitchen
s.how: Soften a diced onion and crushed garlic in butter, add 2 cans crushed tomatoes and simmer 20 minutes, then blend smooth. Make cheddar toasties in butter, cut into fingers and serve with mugs of soup for dunking.

Bring 250ml water and 100g butter to the boil, beat in 150g flour until smooth, then beat in 4 eggs one at a time. Stir in 100g grated gruyere and cracked pepper. Pipe small balls and bake at 200C for 20 minutes until puffed and golden.

m.how: Brown 1kg diced beef chuck and 150g bacon. Add 250g mushrooms and cook until golden, then pour in a bottle of red wine. Simmer for 3 hours until tender and glossy. Serve over mash from 1kg potatoes and plenty of butter.

w.note: the 1970s, when fondue parties were everywhere
w.how: Melt 250g dark chocolate gently with 250ml cream in a fondue pot or small pan. Keep warm at the table. Set out strawberries, marshmallows and cubes of sponge cake on forks for dipping. Very Paris, 1973.

d.how: Fill glasses with crushed ice. Add 30ml blue curacao for the grown-ups, or a few drops of blue colouring for everyone else, and top with cold lemonade. Squeeze in a wedge of lime. It changes depending on who is drinking it.
